identity.name: Potassium adipate
identity.chemical_class: Potassium salt of an aliphatic dicarboxylic acid (adipate salt)

function.mechanism: Provides adipate buffering/acidulant function to adjust and stabilize product acidity (pH) and sourness profile.
common_food_categories: No direct E357 category list identified in retrieved sources
Related adipic-acid CFR categories include baked goods, nonalcoholic beverages, condiments and relishes, dairy analogs, gelatin/puddings, gravies, meat products, and snack foods

adi.basis: No EFSA ADI for E357 identified in the retrieved official EU re-evaluation summary table (status as of 18 Feb 2026); EFSA opinion date/publication/link fields were blank for E357.

efsa.key_finding: E357 is listed as already permitted before 20 January 2009, but the table marks re-evaluation as not completed and gives a deadline of 2018-12-31 with no linked EFSA opinion.

fda.cfr_citation: No direct potassium adipate citation found in Title 21; related adipic acid citations: 21 CFR 184.1009 and 21 CFR 582.1009
fda.notes: FDA eCFR Title 21 and FDA Food Substances database search did not return a direct potassium adipate record in this research run.

adi.basis: Group ADI 0-5 mg/kg bw for adipic acid and its potassium, sodium and ammonium salts (1977 entry); potassium adipate record also contains a 2015 note that provisions were withdrawn at CCFA47 and not re-evaluated.

notable_bans: JECFA record notes provisions for potassium adipate were withdrawn at CCFA47 (Codex context).

concerns.summary: Historical JECFA group toxicology indicates gastrointestinal effects (diarrhoea) in a 2-year rat study at higher dietary concentrations; group ADI was set at 0-5 mg/kg bw.
JECFA 2025 adipate-group exposure commentary indicates conservative exposure estimates can greatly exceed the current group ADI and that updated toxicology re-evaluation is needed.
Direct contemporary potassium-adipate-specific human safety literature is sparse (PubMed exact title/abstract query returned zero records).

no_concern_confirmed: No IARC classification entry was found for potassium adipate or adipic acid in the retrieved IARC classification dataset.
A PubMed toxicology review for adipic acid (indirect evidence) reports low acute oral toxicity and no clear genotoxic/developmental toxicity signal in tested systems.

populations: general consumers under conservative adipate-group exposure scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: Direct E357-only intake estimates were not identified, but JECFA adipate-group 2025 commentary reports potential and substantial exceedances of the current group ADI in conservative scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E357 appears legacy-permitted in EU state-of-play data and has an established JECFA group ADI, but key caveats include incomplete EFSA re-evaluation fields for E357 in the latest retrieved table, sparse direct modern E357 safety literature, and JECFA adipate-group commentary indicating possible ADI exceedance and need for toxicology re-evaluation.
key_factors: EU summary table marks E357 as permitted before 2009 but re-evaluation not completed with no linked EFSA opinion
No direct potassium adipate listing found in retrieved current U.S. Title 21/FDA food-substances query
JECFA group ADI 0-5 mg/kg bw applies to adipic acid and potassium/sodium/ammonium salts
JECFA potassium adipate page includes 2015 note about provision withdrawal at CCFA47
IARC dataset search found no potassium adipate classification
